CVE-2026-47735.description: Arc is an open, SQL-native time-series database for telemetry. Prior to version 26.06.1, Arc's user-SQL validator (`internal/api/query.go:ValidateSQLRequest`) blocked only `read_parquet(` and `arc_partition_agg(` via regex denylist. The broader DuckDB I/O function family — `read_csv_auto`, `read_csv`, `read_json`, `read_json_auto`, `read_text`, `read_blob`, `glob`, `parquet_metadata`, `parquet_schema`, `read_xlsx`, etc. — was not blocked. RBAC table-reference extraction inspected only `FROM`/`JOIN` clauses, so scalar table functions in the `SELECT` list slipped past both layers. This is fixed in 2026.06.1 via a structural sandbox at the DuckDB layer. After lockdown, DuckDB refuses to open any file outside the allowlist and refuses further `INSTALL`/`LOAD`. Already-loaded extensions remain callable. Some workarounds are available. Restrict API access to known-trusted networks via firewall rules or, as a temporary mitigation, add `read_csv*`/`read_json*`/`glob` etc. to `dangerousSQLPattern` in `internal/api/query.go`.

CVE-2026-48105.description: Arc is an open, SQL-native time-series database for telemetry. Prior to version 26.06.1, Arc Enterprise's Raft FSM (`internal/cluster/raft/fsm.go:applyRegisterFile`) accepts attacker-chosen file paths in manifest-registration proposals without validating them against the configured storage backend. The only check is that the path is non-empty. There is no parent-traversal (`..`) rejection, no allowlist of legitimate prefixes, no scheme restriction (`s3://` vs local), and no length bound. This is fixed in 2026.06.1. Some workarounds are available. Restrict cluster network access to known-trusted peers via strict firewall rules, audit the cluster manifest for unexpected paths (any path not matching the configured storage backend root is suspect), and/or disable cluster mode until the fix is available.

CVE-2026-48106.description: Arc is an open, SQL-native time-series database for telemetry. Prior to version 26.06.1, Arc Enterprise's cluster replication receiver at `internal/cluster/replication/receiver.go` validates only the wire-format envelope (length, opcode) of inbound messages. The `MsgReplicateSync` payload itself is accepted without any application-layer authentication — no HMAC, no signature, no per-message nonce. The replication stream is protected at the transport layer by TLS / mTLS, but there is no protection against application-layer message tampering or replay once a peer is on the cluster network. This is fixed in 2026.06.1. Some workarounds are available. Restrict cluster network access to known-trusted peers via strict firewall rules, audit replication logs for unexpected `MsgReplicateSync` traffic, and/or disable cluster mode until the fix is available.

CVE-2026-55098.description: Arc is an open, SQL-native time-series database for telemetry. Prior to the repository-verified 26.06.2 repair, the remediation of `CVE-2026-47735` leaves a cross-database authorization bypass through DuckDB table-valued I/O functions. In `internal/database/sandbox.go`, `allowed_directories` uses `cfg.LocalStorageRoot`, configured by `storage.local_path`, while `enable_external_access=false` blocks access outside that entire multi-tenant root. `GetStoragePath` in `internal/storage/util.go` stores all databases beneath it. In `internal/api/query.go`, `extractTableReferences` skips names followed by an opening parenthesis and `checkQueryPermissions` allows queries with no extracted table references, including tokens with `permissions: []`. The `userSQLReadParquetPattern` denylist catches literal `read_parquet(` and the earlier protection also blocks `arc_partition_agg(`, but misses the `parquet_scan` alias and `glob`, `parquet_metadata`, `parquet_schema`, `read_blob`, `read_csv_auto`, `read_json` and `read_text`. A request to `POST /api/v1/query` using these unblocked functions passes `ValidateSQLRequest` and `convertSQLToStoragePaths` without tenant authorization, allowing reads and enumeration of other databases' time-series data, schema and per-column value-range statistics within the allowlisted root. The sandbox still blocks out-of-root OS files and HTTP SSRF, and the sibling SQLite token database outside the root is not exposed by this mechanism. The earlier 26.06.1 remediation does not comprehensively deny these I/O functions. Repository tag 26.06.2 contains the I/O-function repair and supplies the provisional remediation boundary; conflicting advisory affected-version statements require curator adjudication.

GHSA-4v7m-m7xf-4h6v.title: Cached API tokens remain authorized after expiration
GHSA-4v7m-m7xf-4h6v.description: # Cached API tokens remain authorized after expiration ## Summary Arc's token authentication cache can continue accepting a token after the token's own `expires_at` has passed. `AuthManager.VerifyToken` treats a cache entry as valid solely while its cache TTL is live, so a token first used before expiry remains authorized on subsequent protected requests until cache eviction. The behavior was reproduced against revision `bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2`: the protected request returned 200 before expiry and 200 after expiry, while the same request after cache invalidation returned 401. ## Technical Details The affected path is `NewMiddleware` in `internal/auth/middleware.go`, which extracts the bearer token, calls `AuthManager.VerifyToken`, checks the returned permissions, and invokes the protected handler when verification succeeds. A nil result is converted to HTTP 401, but a non-nil cached `TokenInfo` is trusted and can satisfy a required permission such as `admin`. In `internal/auth/auth.go`, the cache-hit branch at lines 831-837 checks `now.Before(entry.expiresAt)`. That `cacheEntry.expiresAt` is created from `now.Add(am.cacheTTL)` at lines 931-934; it is not the token's expiration time. The database path later checks the token row's `expires_at` at lines 884-888 and copies it to `TokenInfo.ExpiresAt` at lines 910-912. Consequently, cache misses enforce token expiry but cache hits do not. The normal creation API accepts an `expires_in` duration and converts it to `TokenInfo.ExpiresAt`, so this is reachable for supported expiring API tokens rather than requiring malformed database state. The required preconditions are a token that was valid and successfully cached, a token expiration earlier than the cache-entry expiry, and reuse of the same token before cache eviction. No administrative privilege is needed for the post-expiry request; the caller only needs to possess a token that was valid at issuance. The violated invariant is: every successful `VerifyToken` result must be rejected once its `TokenInfo.ExpiresAt` is at or before the current time, regardless of whether verification reaches SQLite or returns from the in-memory cache. The behavior is not intended because the same token receives different authorization results solely from cache state: a cache miss rejects the expired credential, while a live cache entry bypasses that check. ## PoV The focused reproduction invokes the production `NewMiddleware` and `VerifyToken` implementations. Both modes use the same token, the same token hash, and the same non-empty `api_tokens`-shaped database row. The row is returned through the normal `database/sql` driver interface, so the production query, row scan, hash comparison, and expiration check are exercised. The primary mode starts with an empty authentication cache. Its first request reaches the row while it is valid and populates the production cache. After the row's `expires_at` passes, the second request uses the still-live cache entry. The cache is then invalidated and a third request reaches the same expired row. The control mode makes no pre-expiry request; it presents the same expired row through an empty cache and therefore reaches the database expiration check directly. | Mode and request | HTTP status | Database queries / rows | Executed path | | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | | Primary, before expiry | 200 | 1 / 1 | database row, then cache population | | Primary, after expiry with cache live | 200 | 1 / 1 total | cached-entry branch | | Primary, after `InvalidateCache` | 401 | 2 / 2 total | same database row, then database expiration check | | Control, after expiry with cache empty | 401 | 1 / 1 | same database row, then database expiration check | The primary result is therefore `before=200`, `after=200`, `cache_miss=401`, with `cache_ttl=5m0s`. The control result is `status_after_expiry=401`, with one query and one returned row. The control is a negative control for the database expiration branch: it is not an empty-result or database-error case. ## PoC The complete, self-contained setup and test are in Appendix A. The script copies `auth.go` and the first 243 lines of `middleware.go` from the pinned checkout, writes the module file, all focused-package shims, the database-row driver, the test, and the outcome paths. It does not require network access or any package download. Run it from a checkout of the target revision: ```sh git -C /absolute/path/to/arc checkout bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2 ARC_REPO=/absolute/path/to/arc sh appendix-a-cache-expiry.sh ``` The script verifies the revision before copying source. It runs both modes with the following explicit environment; the reproduction root is a neutral caller-selected path: ```sh POC_ROOT=/path/to/reproduction SOURCE_REVISION=bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2 TARGET_SHA256=717fc9766808fb776682530187107c98c255a8382a135c523274a643dc0d79f8 OUTCOME_PATH='$POC_ROOT/outcomes/primary.json' # or control.json CACHE_EXPIRY_MODE=primary # or control ``` Expected test-process output for each mode is a passing Go test. The security observation is recorded in the JSON outcome, not in the process exit status. The following is an abridged excerpt from each run with variable durations omitted: ```text === RUN TestCachedTokenExpiry --- PASS: TestCachedTokenExpiry PASS ok github.com/basekick-labs/arc/internal/auth ``` The primary outcome has `result=violation`, `signal=expired cached token remained authorized`, `before=200`, `after=200`, `cache_miss=401`, `database_queries=2`, and `database_rows=2`. Its reachability route is: ```text NewMiddleware -> VerifyToken -> database row (before expiry) -> cache; cached-entry branch (after expiry); InvalidateCache -> database row -> database expiration check ``` The control outcome has `result=pass`, `signal=expired database credential rejected`, `status_after_expiry=401`, `database_queries=1`, and `database_rows=1`. Its reachability route is: ```text NewMiddleware -> VerifyToken -> database query -> matching database row -> database expiration check ``` The timestamps and test durations vary between runs; the statuses, query/row counts, routes, and outcome signals are the proof conditions. ## Impact An untrusted remote caller who possesses a previously valid Arc API token can continue authenticating after its configured expiration, crossing Arc's authentication and authorization boundary for as long as the corresponding cache entry remains live. The caller retains every permission encoded in that token, so an expired token with write, delete, or administrative permissions can continue to authorize those protected actions during the stale-cache window. A five-minute window was demonstrated; the maximum window is controlled by the configured authentication cache TTL and can be longer. This is an expiration-boundary bypass, not a privilege-escalation path: the attacker does not gain permissions the token never had. CWE-613 (Insufficient Session Expiration) is the appropriate classification because a credential remains accepted after its intended validity period. The advisory metadata's typed high severity is justified by the retained ability to perform protected actions, including administrative actions, during the cache window. Revocation or cache invalidation causes the database path to reject the expired token, limiting the finding to cached reuse before eviction or TTL expiry. The caller must already possess a token that was valid at issuance, and only the pinned revision was tested; no fixed revision was available for comparison. ## Suggested Fix Make the cache-hit path enforce the same token-expiration invariant as the database path before returning `entry.info`. Under the appropriate cache lock, reject and evict an entry whose `TokenInfo.ExpiresAt` is at or before `now`, or fall through to the normal database validation path so the expired row returns 401. As a defense in depth measure, set each cache entry's TTL to the earlier of `now + cacheTTL` and the token's `ExpiresAt`; that bound alone should not replace the explicit check at read time. Add a regression test that creates or seeds a short-lived token, authenticates it once before expiry, reuses it after expiry while the cache TTL is still live, and asserts HTTP 401. The test should also invalidate the cache and assert that the same post-expiry request remains 401 on a cache miss, and should cover non-expiring tokens and the exact expiration boundary. ## Affected Package/Versions - Package: `github.com/basekick-labs/arc` (Go module). - Vulnerable tested revision: `bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2`. - Affected range: only the tested revision above; no broader release range is asserted. - Patched version: none identified or tested. - Vulnerable functions: `internal/auth.(*AuthManager).VerifyToken` and `internal/auth.NewMiddleware`. ## Advisory History The repository's public history includes [GHSA-wwfh-qrfq-6f8g](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/security/advisories/GHSA-wwfh-qrfq-6f8g), covering unauthenticated Raft transport and admin-token forgery; [GHSA-wmjj-g8xc-6hwr](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/security/advisories/GHSA-wmjj-g8xc-6hwr), covering an authenticated query-parameter bypass that can read other tenants' databases; and [GHSA-p378-jp5r-gpgw / CVE-2026-55678](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/security/advisories/GHSA-p378-jp5r-gpgw), covering unauthenticated cluster-node admission when the shared secret is unset. None of these published records describes a cached `VerifyToken` result bypassing `expires_at`; this finding is distinct because the in-memory cache returns a `TokenInfo` after its own `ExpiresAt`, while the corresponding cache-miss/database path rejects the same token. No earlier submitted, ready-for-review, or completed-but-unsubmitted report for this behavior was available in the reviewed report set. ## References - [Token verification and cache handling at the tested revision](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/blob/bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2/internal/auth/auth.go#L823-L937) - [Authentication middleware at the tested revision](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/blob/bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2/internal/auth/middleware.go#L46-L168) - [Expiring-token creation and update handling at the tested revision](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/blob/bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2/internal/api/auth_routes.go#L82-L161) - [CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/613.html) ## Appendix ### A. GHSA-9rgq-j585-5fhq.title: Replacement-scan guard covered only FROM and JOIN: a path literal after TABLE/SUMMARIZE/DESCRIBE/PIVOT/UNPIVOT reads any tenant's data with no permission check
GHSA-9rgq-j585-5fhq.description: ## Impact Arc disables DuckDB's replacement scans: a path in table position must be refused, because the permission check authorizes *measurements*, and a bare path is not one. `ValidateSQLRequest` enforced that only for the `FROM` and `JOIN` keywords. DuckDB also introduces a relation after **`TABLE`**, **`SUMMARIZE`**, **`DESCRIBE`**, **`PIVOT`** and **`UNPIVOT`**, each of which accepts a path there and reads the file. Arc's table-position scanner (`walkTablePositions`, `internal/api/table_position.go`) armed only on `from` and `join`, so none of those positions was ever examined. The consequence, on every endpoint that accepts user SQL: ``` TABLE '<storage-root>/<other-tenant>/<measurement>/**/*.parquet' -> validator: accepted -> permission check: EMPTY reference set, which is allowed outright -> rewriter: statement passed through verbatim -> DuckDB: returns the rows ``` A read-capable token reads any Parquet file inside the DuckDB sandbox allowlist, with **no grant, no header and no license required**, and with no permission check performed at all — the extractor produces no reference, so there is nothing to authorize. Variants, all confirmed: - `SUMMARIZE '<glob>'` returns min, max, count and approximate distinct count for **every column**, which is a compact exfiltration primitive rather than a single value. - `PIVOT '<glob>' ON <column> USING count(*)` returns the column's **values as column names**. - `SELECT v.c FROM <granted>.<measurement> o, (TABLE '<glob>') v` joins the victim's data into an otherwise authorized query, so the check set is non-empty and looks ordinary. - `SELECT 1 FROM <granted> WHERE EXISTS (TABLE '<glob>')` is a boolean oracle, and works through the row-count estimate endpoint as well. ## Scope The DuckDB sandbox itself holds: paths outside the allowlist are refused with `Permission Error: … file system operations are disabled by configuration`. The reachable set is therefore the allowlist, which is the **entire local storage root** — every database and measurement in the deployment — plus the temp, upload and compaction directories, and the configured object-store prefix. Other tenants' staged uploads are included. Affected endpoints: every route that accepts user SQL, including the JSON, msgpack and Arrow query endpoints, the row-count estimate endpoint, and the per-measurement GET endpoint through its `where` parameter. Not affected: ingest paths, which construct no SQL from user input. ## Root cause Authorization is derived by scanning SQL text for keywords rather than by parsing it. The set of keywords that introduce a relation is a property of DuckDB's grammar, and the scanner's list was a subset of it. A keyword the scanner does not know fails **open**: no table position means no reference, and no reference means an empty authorization set, which is permitted. This is the fourth instance of the replacement-scan class, after CVE-2026-47735, GHSA-93cm-2v4m-c56c and GHSA-w8x2-cccw-25f7. Each previous round closed the spelling that had been reported. ## Patch The scanner now arms on `table`, `summarize`, `describe`, `pivot` and `unpivot` in addition to `from` and `join`, so a literal in any of those positions is refused by the same guard that already covered `FROM`. The arming is deliberately narrower than for `from`/`join`: those keywords mark the clause as able to continue across a comma, and none of the new forms does. Arming that state for them would make a later comma a table position and refuse legitimate statements such as `PIVOT t ON c IN ('a','b')`. A regression test covers each keyword, in each nesting position (derived table, comma cross-join, JOIN, scalar subquery, `EXISTS`, CTE body), in mixed case, and with whitespace or a comment between the keyword and the literal — alongside a set of legitimate statements using the same keywords that must keep working. **This closes the keywords DuckDB has today; it does not change the shape of the defence.** A future DuckDB relation keyword would fail open again. The durable fix is to derive the relation set from a parse tree rather than from keyword scanning, tracked publicly as Basekick-Labs/arc#764 and #491. ## Workaround None within Arc. A reverse proxy could reject request bodies matching those keywords, but that is brittle against whitespace, comments and case. Upgrading is the remedy. ## Credit Found internally during a security review of the query authorization path.

GHSA-h3rq-5r29-2wrh.title: RBAC bypass: three normalisation divergences let a query read measurements the permission check never saw
GHSA-h3rq-5r29-2wrh.description:
## Impact Arc decides twice which measurements a query touches. The RBAC extractor normalises the SQL and builds the set of measurements to authorize; the query rewriter normalises it again and decides which names become Parquet paths. Any divergence between the two lets a query read a measurement the permission check never saw. The amplifier: **a query whose extracted reference set is empty is authorized outright** (`internal/api/query.go:1593-1597`). So a divergence that empties the set is a total bypass, not a partial one. Three divergences were present. Each requires RBAC enabled, a valid read token, and an `x-arc-database` header — the documented way for a client to target a database, and not itself subject to a grant. ### 1. The CTE pattern fired with no `WITH` in the query (no grant required) `patternCTENames` (`internal/api/query.go:98`) has a second alternative, `,\s*(\w+)...AS\s*\(`, with no `WITH` anchor. A multi-definition `WINDOW` clause matches it. `extractTableReferences` consulted that pattern unconditionally (`:1396`). Every rewriter consulted it only after finding a `WITH` keyword (`:2977`, `:3932`, `:3975`), and the two single-table fast paths have no CTE handling at all. ``` x-arc-database: sensitive SELECT * FROM secret WINDOW w AS (), secret AS () check set = [] -> allowed outright read set = [sensitive/secret] -> on both the header and parallel paths ``` **No grant of any kind was required**, for any measurement in any database the caller names in the header. A variant naming a second, real table needed only that table's grant and read both: ``` SELECT * FROM cpu a, secret b WINDOW w AS (), secret AS () check set = [sensitive/cpu] read set = [sensitive/cpu, sensitive/secret] ``` That also defeated the comma cross-join permission check added in #978. ### 2. `WITH` followed by a newline or tab was not recognised as a CTE clause (no grant required) The extractor matches `WITH` as a word followed by any whitespace (`\s` includes `
`, `	`, ``); three rewriter gates searched for the literal `'with '`, with a space. ``` WITH
t AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM t check set = [] -> allowed outright read set = [sensitive/t] ``` Both the header rewriter and the parallel fast path were affected. The fast path has no CTE handling of its own, so it rewrote the name even when the CTE body was a plain `SELECT`. ### 3. The single-table fast paths located `FROM` with no leading word boundary (no grant required) `isSingleTableQuery` and both fast paths searched for the literal `'from '`; the extractor's `patternSimpleTable` (`:71`) requires ` FROM`. A digit is an identifier byte, so the boundary test declines where the plain search matches. DuckDB lexes `1from` as `1` then `FROM`. ``` SELECT *,1from secret check set = [] -> allowed outright read set = [sensitive/secret] ``` Confirmed for integer, float and exponent literals, with `ORDER BY` / `LIMIT` appended. Adding a quote or comment routes to the slow path, whose regexes are boundary-correct, so a payload simply omits them. ## Reachability - Requires **RBAC enabled** — the Enterprise multi-tenant authorization boundary. With RBAC disabled there is no per-measurement authorization to bypass. - Requires a **valid authentication token**. This is horizontal privilege escalation, not an unauthenticated read. - Requires the **`x-arc-database` header**. Without it, `convertSQLToStoragePaths` extracts CTE names unconditionally and uses only boundary-correct regexes, so the check and read sets always agreed. - **No configuration key gates any of it**: the affected transforms run unconditionally on `POST /api/v1/query`. ## Patch 1. The `WITH` predicate moves **inside** `extractCTENames`, so all five callers share one expression and the extractor and rewriters cannot disagree about whether to consult the CTE pattern. The redundant outer gate on the header path is removed. Returning an empty set is safe: the only writes to that map are inside `extractCTENames`, and every other site only reads it. 2. The three gates match `WITH` as a word, via the `containsSQLWord` helper that #978 introduced for the identical mistake with `JOIN`. A measurement named `with_history` is still a measurement. 3. The fast paths' `FROM` searches require a leading word boundary (`indexSQLTokenStart` / `countSQLTokenStart`). Only the leading boundary is enforced, so routing is unchanged for shapes that already worked. Tested against `xfrom`, `1from`, `from_host`, and the keyword at index 0. A regression suite, `internal/api/rbac_normalisation_parity_test.go`, asserts the invariant directly — the check set is never smaller than the read set — across all three rewriters. Each fix was verified by reverting it alone and confirming its own cases fail. A fourth, lower-severity divergence in the same seam is fixed alongside: the extractor skipped a table-valued function on space/tab/CR/LF while the rewriter trimmed only space and tab, so `FROM generate_series
(1, 10)` was a function to the check and a measurement to the rewriter. DuckDB rejects the resulting SQL rather than reading anything, so that one was never a bypass. ## Workaround None that preserves functionality. Deployments that can do so may strip or reject the `x-arc-database` header at the proxy until patched; queries then resolve against the `default` database only, which is not affected by any of the three. ## Credit Found internally while verifying that #827 — a different case-folding defect in the same seam — was already fixed in 26.09.2. All three divergences predate that fix and #978.

GHSA-mcqm-h7hj-99fg.title: RBAC read and write restrictions were unreachable, and the database listing endpoints had no authorization at all
GHSA-mcqm-h7hj-99fg.description: ## Impact Two authorization decisions that never took effect. ### RBAC read and write restrictions were unreachable On an RBAC denial, the permission check fell back to the token's coarse permission list, which performs no database or measurement filtering. At the same time the route middleware (`RequireRead`, `RequireWrite`) consulted only that same coarse list and never RBAC. For an RBAC denial to take effect, a token had to: - hold the coarse `read` bit, to pass the middleware, and - **not** hold it, for the fallback to decline Those are contradictory. **No read or write path in Arc could be narrowed by RBAC under any configuration.** A token carrying `read` read every database and measurement in the deployment regardless of its grants; a token deliberately created with no coarse permissions — the documented way to request an RBAC-only token — was refused by the middleware before RBAC was ever consulted. Affected: query permission checks, the per-measurement endpoint, `SHOW DATABASES`, `SHOW TABLES FROM <db>`, the measurement listing, and the shared write-permission check used by every ingest path. No test covered it. The RBAC test suite is constructed with no license client, so the function containing the fallback is never reached, and the API-level tests use a mock with no fallback — a mock stricter than production. ### The database listing endpoints had no authorization at all `GET /api/v1/databases`, `/api/v1/databases/:name` and `/api/v1/databases/:name/measurements` were registered with no route middleware and no permission check, while the corresponding mutating routes were admin-gated. Any valid token — including a write-only ingest token — could enumerate every database and measurement name in the deployment, and could probe which databases exist via the 404-versus-200 distinction. ## Patch Enforcement is now decided by a token's **team memberships**, not by the license: 1. coarse `admin` → allowed (break-glass; otherwise an admin token added to a team would lock itself out of its own tooling) 2. has team memberships → RBAC is authoritative and a denial is **final** 3. no team memberships → coarse permissions, unchanged — the 'backward compatible with OSS tokens' guarantee the original RBAC work made Enforcement no longer consults the license anywhere. That is deliberate and important: a license is valid only while `active` or in its grace period, and the client is dropped entirely when validation fails at startup, so a lapsed trial, a revoked key or a prolonged outage would otherwise switch enforcement off and silently widen every tenant token to full read at whatever hour it expired. The license still gates RBAC **management**, so a lapse removes the ability to change grants, never the grants' effect. A failure to load a token's grants now denies rather than falling through. The middleware half ships with it. A resource-scoped middleware that consults RBAC already existed in the codebase and was wired to nothing; it is now used by the listing routes, so an RBAC-only token can reach a handler and be scoped by its grants. The three listing routes now require read authority and check it per database: listing every database requires a grant covering every database, matching `SHOW DATABASES`, and the scoped routes require a grant for the named database, matching `SHOW TABLES FROM <db>`. The permission check runs before any storage access, so the existence probe is closed too. ## Upgrade notes This changes behaviour for deployments that have RBAC configured, and for tokens lacking the coarse `read` permission: - A token with team memberships is now restricted to its grants. Previously it was not restricted at all. Review grants before upgrading. - A write-only or permissionless token can no longer enumerate database or measurement names. - A token scoped to specific databases receives `403` from `GET /api/v1/databases` and must name its database. Client tooling that lists databases needs to handle that. ## Credit Found internally while reviewing the query authorization path.

GHSA-p2rx-8p53-cqh3.title: JoinRequest HMAC Omits Security-Sensitive Fields, Enabling Cluster Topology Tampering
GHSA-p2rx-8p53-cqh3.description: # JoinRequest HMAC Omits Security-Sensitive Fields, Enabling Cluster Topology Tampering ## Summary Arc's cluster join authentication authenticates only the message type, nonce, node ID, cluster name, and timestamp, leaving security-sensitive JoinRequest metadata outside the HMAC. In a supported TLS-disabled cluster, an attacker who can modify inter-node traffic can preserve a valid HMAC while changing the joining node's role and advertised API, coordinator, or Raft addresses; the pinned revision accepts those values into cluster state. ## Technical Details The shipped join path is `tryJoinViaSeed` → `handlePeerConnection` → `handleJoinRequest`. The sender constructs a JoinRequest containing `NodeName`, `Role`, `RaftAddr`, `APIAddr`, `CoordAddr`, `Version`, and `CoreCount`, then computes the tag with only `req.NodeID`, `req.ClusterName`, and `req.AuthTimestamp` (plus the nonce and message type): ```go req.AuthHMAC = security.ComputeHMAC(c.cfg.SharedSecret, security.MsgTypeJoin, nonce, req.NodeID, req.ClusterName, req.AuthTimestamp) ``` `ComputeHMAC` documents the canonical payload as `msgType \x00 nonce \x00 nodeID \x00 clusterName \x00 timestamp`. `ValidateHMAC` recomputes exactly that payload, so changing `Role`, `NodeName`, `RaftAddr`, `APIAddr`, `CoordAddr`, `Version`, or `CoreCount` does not invalidate the tag. The receiving handler validates the tag and then consumes the unsigned fields as security and routing state: ```go if err := security.ValidateHMAC( c.cfg.SharedSecret, security.MsgTypeJoin, req.AuthNonce, req.NodeID, req.ClusterName, req.AuthTimestamp, req.AuthHMAC, security.HMACTimestampTolerance, ); err != nil { return } node := NewNode(req.NodeID, req.NodeName, ParseRole(req.Role), req.ClusterName) node.SetAddresses(req.CoordAddr, req.APIAddr) node.SetVersion(req.Version) ``` When Raft is configured, the same handler passes `req.RaftAddr` to `AddVoter` and copies the unsigned role and advertised addresses into the Raft node metadata. Without Raft, the node is registered directly. Thus the accepted message changes cluster membership metadata even though its shared-secret authentication remains valid. The relevant preconditions are a licensed cluster-enabled deployment with a shared secret and TLS disabled, plus an attacker able to modify the plaintext coordinator connection. The attacker does not need the shared secret or a new node ID: the MAC-bound node ID, cluster name, nonce, timestamp, and tag remain unchanged. A changed node ID is rejected by the same validator. ## PoV Start with a valid JoinRequest and retain the following fields unchanged: `NodeID`, `ClusterName`, `AuthNonce`, `AuthTimestamp`, and `AuthHMAC`. Change only fields omitted from the authenticated payload: ```json { 'Role': 'reader -> writer', 'APIAddr': '10.0.0.2:8080 -> attacker.example:8080', 'CoordAddr': '10.0.0.2:9100 -> attacker.example:9100', 'RaftAddr': '10.0.0.2:9200 -> attacker.example:9200' } ``` The receiver accepts the unchanged tag and registers the joining node with the attacker-selected role and addresses. As a negative control, change `NodeID` while keeping the tag stale; validation rejects the request and no node is registered under the changed ID. ## PoC Check out the tested revision, save Appendix A as `internal/cluster/join_hmac_reproducer_test.go`, and run: ```sh git clone https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc.git cd arc git checkout bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2 go test ./internal/cluster -run '^TestJoinHMACFieldMutationReproducer$' -count=1 -v ``` The test uses `net.Pipe` to invoke the shipped `handlePeerConnection` dispatcher and sends a real protocol JoinRequest through it. It does not need credentials or an external service. Abridged output, with file and line prefixes omitted, is: ```text mutated: result=violation signal='unsigned JoinRequest role and advertised addresses accepted into coordinator registry' control: result=pass signal='MAC-bound NodeID mutation rejected' ``` The test against revision `bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2` exercised the primary mutation and the MAC-bound NodeID control; both completed successfully and the request reached `handleJoinRequest`. ## Impact This crosses Arc's cluster authentication and topology boundary: an on-path attacker can promote a joining node from reader to writer and redirect the node's coordinator/API metadata without knowing the shared secret. With Raft enabled, the same primitive also supplies the voter address and replicated node metadata. The demonstrated consequence is unauthorized cluster topology and routing-integrity modification; deployments using TLS for the inter-node connection are not covered by this PoC. The issue is CWE-345, Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity. A conservative CVSS v3.1 vector is `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N` (Medium, 5.7): exploitation requires an on-path position on a plaintext inter-node connection, while the demonstrated high-integrity effect is limited to cluster membership, topology, and routing state controlled by the unsigned fields. The vector assigns no confidentiality or availability impact; this report does not claim code execution, direct data disclosure, or a service outage. ## Suggested Fix Create one canonical JoinRequest authentication payload and use it from both the sender and validator. It should include every field later used to establish membership, role, topology, or routing: `NodeID`, `NodeName`, `Role`, `ClusterName`, `RaftAddr`, `APIAddr`, `CoordAddr`, `Version`, `CoreCount`, the message type, nonce, and timestamp. Keep the encoding unambiguous and compare the resulting HMAC with the existing constant-time path. Add regression coverage that changes each security-sensitive field independently after signing and verifies rejection, while an unchanged request succeeds. Exercise both the no-Raft registry path and the Raft path, and retain a control that changes a currently MAC-bound field to prevent accidental weakening of the validator. ## Affected Package/Versions - Package: `github.com/basekick-labs/arc` (Go module). - Vulnerable revision: `bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2`. - Current head at the tested revision: vulnerable. - No patched revision was tested, and no broader version range is inferred. ## Advisory History Arc's public history includes [GHSA-p378-jp5r-gpgw (CVE-2026-55678)](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/security/advisories/GHSA-p378-jp5r-gpgw), “Unauthenticated cluster node admission when `cluster.shared_secret` is unset,” which reports that a coordinator accepts a join when the shared secret is empty and lists a fix in 26.06.2. The related [issue #366](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/issues/366), “security(enterprise): unauthenticated cluster node joins — no shared secret or mTLS,” describes the same missing-authentication condition before that fix. [Pull request #383](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/pull/383), “feat(cluster): stable node identity and graceful leave broadcast,” added HMAC authentication to `LeaveNotify` and describes it as matching the JoinRequest authentication pattern. Other directly related cluster-authentication advisories include [GHSA-wfgr-8x84-22q7 (CVE-2026-48106)](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/security/advisories/GHSA-wfgr-8x84-22q7), concerning unauthenticated `MsgReplicateSync` payloads from TLS-trusted peers, and [GHSA-wwfh-qrfq-6f8g](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/security/advisories/GHSA-wwfh-qrfq-6f8g), concerning missing application-layer authentication on the Raft transport. Those advisories cover different messages and fix surfaces. This finding requires a valid shared-secret HMAC and exploits `JoinRequest` role and address fields that are not included in that HMAC; it is not the earlier empty-secret admission flaw. A check of prior report records found no submitted, ready-for-review, or completed-but-unsubmitted report covering this JoinRequest field-omission boundary. ## References - [JoinRequest definition at the tested revision](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/blob/bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2/internal/cluster/protocol/messages.go#L127-L142) - [JoinRequest signing in `tryJoinViaSeed`](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/blob/bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2/internal/cluster/coordinator.go#L904-L953) - [Peer dispatch in `handlePeerConnection`](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/blob/bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2/internal/cluster/coordinator.go#L1022-L1058) - [Join validation and state registration in `handleJoinRequest`](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/blob/bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2/internal/cluster/coordinator.go#L1088-L1185) - [HMAC payload construction and validation](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/blob/bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2/internal/cluster/security/auth.go#L42-L64) - [HMAC freshness and verification](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/blob/bfd757708cd50745306f083f5de9d2d3fcfc88c2/internal/cluster/security/auth.go#L103-L121) - [Public security-advisory listing](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/security/advisories) ## Appendix A: Standalone reproducer ```go package cluster import ( 'io' 'net' 'testing' 'time' 'github.com/basekick-labs/arc/internal/cluster/protocol' 'github.com/basekick-labs/arc/internal/cluster/security' 'github.com/basekick-labs/arc/internal/config' 'github.com/rs/zerolog' ) const ( reproducerSecret = 'join-probe-shared-secret' reproducerCluster = 'join-probe-cluster' reproducerNodeID = 'joining-node' reproducerNonce = 'join-probe-nonce' ) func reproducerCoordinator() *Coordinator { logger := zerolog.New(io.Discard) local := NewNode('leader-node', 'leader', RoleWriter, reproducerCluster) local.UpdateState(StateHealthy) return &Coordinator{ cfg: &config.ClusterConfig{ClusterName: reproducerCluster, SharedSecret: reproducerSecret}, registry: NewRegistry(&RegistryConfig{LocalNode: local, Logger: logger}), localNode: local, logger: logger, } } func reproducerRequest() *protocol.JoinRequest { timestamp := time.Now().Unix() req := &protocol.JoinRequest{ NodeID: reproducerNodeID, NodeName: 'joining-node', Role: 'reader', ClusterName: reproducerCluster, RaftAddr: '10.0.0.2:9200', APIAddr: '10.0.0.2:8080', CoordAddr: '10.0.0.2:9100', Version: '1.0.0', CoreCount: 1, AuthNonce: reproducerNonce, AuthTimestamp: timestamp, } req.AuthHMAC = security.ComputeHMAC(reproducerSecret, security.MsgTypeJoin, req.AuthNonce, req.NodeID, req.ClusterName, req.AuthTimestamp) return req } func sendReproducerJoin(t *testing.T, c *Coordinator, req *protocol.JoinRequest) { t.Helper() server, client := net.Pipe() done := make(chan struct{}) go func() { c.handlePeerConnection(server); close(done) }() if err := protocol.SendMessage(client, protocol.NewJoinRequest(req), 2*time.Second); err != nil { t.Fatalf('send JoinRequest: %v', err) } if _, err := protocol.ReceiveMessage(client, 2*time.Second); err != nil { t.Fatalf('receive JoinResponse: %v', err) } _ = client.Close() select { case <-done: case <-time.After(2 * time.Second): t.Fatal('join handler did not finish') } } func TestJoinHMACFieldMutationReproducer(t *testing.T) { t.Run('mutated_unsigned_fields', func(t *testing.T) { c := reproducerCoordinator() req := reproducerRequest() req.Role = 'writer' req.APIAddr = 'attacker.example:8080' req.CoordAddr = 'attacker.example:9100' req.RaftAddr = 'attacker.example:9200' sendReproducerJoin(t, c, req) node, accepted := c.registry.Get(reproducerNodeID) if !accepted || node.Role != RoleWriter || node.APIAddress != 'attacker.example:8080' || node.Address != 'attacker.example:9100' { t.Fatalf('mutated fields were not accepted: accepted=%v node=%+v', accepted, node) } t.Log(`mutated: result=violation signal='unsigned JoinRequest role and advertised addresses accepted into coordinator registry'`) }) t.Run('bound_node_id_control', func(t *testing.T) { c := reproducerCoordinator() req := reproducerRequest() req.NodeID = 'tampered-node' sendReproducerJoin(t, c, req) if _, accepted := c.registry.Get('tampered-node'); accepted { t.Fatal('MAC-bound NodeID mutation was accepted') } t.Log(`control: result=pass signal='MAC-bound NodeID mutation rejected'`) }) } ```

GHSA-qcf2-6hm7-62c5.title: GET /api/v1/query/:measurement authorized only its path parameters, so a subquery in the `where` parameter read another tenant's measurement
GHSA-qcf2-6hm7-62c5.description: ## Impact `GET /api/v1/query/:measurement` authorized only the database and measurement named in its route and query string. It then assembled `SELECT * FROM <db>.<measurement> WHERE <where> ORDER BY … LIMIT …` from a user-supplied `where` parameter and handed the whole statement to the query rewriter, which resolves table references in **any** table position — including inside that fragment. ``` GET /api/v1/query/cpu?database=db1&where=1%3D(SELECT%20count(*)%20FROM%20db2.secrets) authorized: db1/cpu read: db1/cpu AND db2/secrets ``` No `x-arc-database` header and no license are required. The endpoint returns row counts and rows, so the fragment works as a boolean oracle (`WHERE 1=(SELECT count(*) FROM <victim>)`) and as a string-prefix oracle (`WHERE (SELECT min(c) FROM <victim>) LIKE 'T%'`), giving character-by-character read of another tenant's column. `validateWhereClauseQuery` did not prevent it: it is a substring blocklist for `;`, comment markers and DDL/DML keywords, and does not stop a nested read. Enumerating read syntaxes would not have worked either — DuckDB spells a table reference in a scalar subquery three ways (`(SELECT c FROM t)`, `(FROM t)`, `(TABLE t)`), and `FROM` is legal inside `EXTRACT`, `SUBSTRING` and `TRIM`. ## Patch The endpoint now authorizes every table reference in the assembled statement, not just the one named in the route. `checkQueryPermissions` was split so the database that **bare** references resolve to is supplied by the caller: this route takes its database from `?database=`, builds fully-qualified SQL and gives the rewriter an empty header, so bare names in `where` resolve to `default` and must be checked as `default`. That detail is load-bearing. Passing the `x-arc-database` header instead — the obvious implementation — would authorize `<header>/x` while the query read `default/x`, reintroducing the same class of defect in the fix itself. A regression test pins it. ## Credit Found internally while reviewing the query authorization path.

GHSA-w6w2-x8xv-q8x2.title: Authenticated query() SQL bypass in Arc estimate endpoint enables cross-tenant Parquet reads
GHSA-w6w2-x8xv-q8x2.description:
# Authenticated query() SQL bypass in Arc estimate endpoint enables cross-tenant Parquet reads ## Summary An authenticated read principal can hide executable SQL inside DuckDB's `query()` table function when calling `POST /api/v1/query/estimate`. Arc validates and authorizes only the outer SQL text, so the nested SQL reaches DuckDB without the filesystem-I/O checks or table-reference RBAC checks. On revision `9dda675b9032bf2331a07c1781ebf624f41c6cde`, the mutated request reached the estimate handler's database sink instead of returning the expected `403`, and the same target build executed a nested replacement scan in its storage path. A path inside Arc's shared storage root can therefore cross tenant/database boundaries; the exact tested scope is one vulnerable revision. ## Technical Details `internal/api/query.go:1409-1432` registers `POST /api/v1/query/estimate` behind read authentication and the replication-readiness gate. `estimateQuery` (`internal/api/query.go:3944-4148`) parses the JSON `sql` field, calls `ValidateSQLRequest`, checks `checkQueryPermissions`, transforms the outer statement, wraps it as `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (<converted SQL>) AS t`, and executes it with `h.db.QueryContext`. `ValidateSQLRequest` (`internal/api/query.go:2164-2302`) strips comments and masks literals before rejecting dangerous statements, filesystem-I/O table-function names, and replacement-scan syntax. It does not parse SQL strings passed to DuckDB's dynamic `query()` table function. The permission path (`checkQueryPermissions` and `extractTableReferences` at `internal/api/query.go:1107-1315`) skips names followed by `(` as table-valued functions; consequently the outer `query(...)` contributes no nested database, measurement, or file reference. The transformation step also processes the outer statement, not the SQL string that DuckDB parses later. This violates the invariant that every user-controlled SQL path must account for every filesystem read and referenced tenant before DuckDB execution. It is unintended because the validator's own security comments reserve filesystem-reading SQL for Arc's identity-aware transformation layer and state that user SQL must not contain it. The precondition is a valid low-privilege read token whose request body is attacker-controlled; administrator authorization is not required. ## PoV The tested route mutation changed the second request-body occurrence of the existing cross-database vector from `SELECT * FROM /* sneaky */ otherdb.cpu` to the following outer query. The inner SQL is `SELECT*FROM'/x'` after DuckDB parses the escaped quote characters; `/x` is a neutral placeholder for a replacement-scan path. ```http POST /api/v1/query/estimate HTTP/1.1 Authorization: Bearer <read token scoped to default> Content-Type: application/json {'sql':'SELECT*FROM query('SELECT*FROM''/x''')'} ``` The outer statement contains no ordinary table reference for `checkQueryPermissions` to authorize, while DuckDB is still asked to parse and execute the inner string. Replacing `/x` with an in-root path belonging to another database gives the same primitive against Arc's shared storage allowlist; the scope limitation is that this finding does not claim an escape outside that allowlist. ## PoC The following commands describe the target-test reproduction. Run them from the repository/module root—the directory containing `go.mod` and `internal/api`—and save Appendix A as `./patcher.go` in that same directory (`<module-root>/patcher.go`). Build the test binary from the pinned revision, then run the attack variant after applying the helper. The control variant runs the unmodified binary. ```sh go test -c ./internal/api -o api-security.test go run patcher.go api-security.test ./api-security.test -test.run '^(TestDeleteOldFiles_DryRun|TestEstimateQuery_RBAC_CommentBypassFixed)$' -test.v go test -c ./internal/api -o api-security-control.test ./api-security-control.test -test.run '^(TestDeleteOldFiles_DryRun|TestEstimateQuery_RBAC_CommentBypassFixed)$' -test.v ``` The attack command produced these reproduced lines: ```text === RUN TestEstimateQuery_RBAC_CommentBypassFixed query_rbac_test.go:406: expected 403 (comment-hidden table ref must still be checked), got 500: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference --- FAIL: TestEstimateQuery_RBAC_CommentBypassFixed (0.00s) === RUN TestDeleteOldFiles_DryRun --- PASS: TestDeleteOldFiles_DryRun (0.02s) FAIL ``` The `500` is the test harness's nil-database sink signal: the request passed validation and RBAC far enough to call the database, rather than being denied with `403`. It is not presented as the production response behavior. The nested storage execution is independently shown by the passing `TestDeleteOldFiles_DryRun` after its direct `read_parquet` statement (`internal/api/retention.go:916-930`) was changed to use `query()` over a replacement scan. The unmodified negative control produced: ```text === RUN TestEstimateQuery_RBAC_CommentBypassFixed --- PASS: TestEstimateQuery_RBAC_CommentBypassFixed (0.01s) === RUN TestDeleteOldFiles_DryRun --- PASS: TestDeleteOldFiles_DryRun (0.19s) PASS ``` The control therefore preserves both expected behaviors: direct cross-database SQL is denied and the ordinary retention test still succeeds. The test image used Go's pinned execution environment with the target revision `9dda675b9032bf2331a07c1781ebf624f41c6cde`; no network access is required. ## Impact On an RBAC-enabled multi-tenant deployment, a user with a valid read token can submit an outer `query()` call whose inner SQL invokes `read_parquet` or a replacement scan against another database's Parquet files within the configured storage root. Arc's SQL validator and table extractor do not see the nested file path, while DuckDB executes it after the checks. This is a cross-tenant confidentiality boundary violation affecting any tenant that can reach the authenticated estimate endpoint; it does not require an administrator grant. The structured classification is CWE-862 (Missing Authorization) with CVSS 3.1 vector `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N`. The vector reflects a network-reachable authenticated attack with low privileges, no user interaction, changed security scope, and high confidentiality impact, with no demonstrated integrity or availability impact. The route-sink probe and nested storage test establish the bypass and execution primitive; they do not claim arbitrary operating-system file access or show a production data response, and only the pinned revision was tested. ## Suggested Fix The smallest guard for the demonstrated route is to reject DuckDB's `query()` dynamic-SQL table function in attacker-controlled input inside `ValidateSQLRequest`, before `checkQueryPermissions` and `QueryContext`. If dynamic SQL is a required feature, recursively parse every constant inner SQL string, apply the same filesystem/replacement-scan validation, and merge every nested table and resolved file reference into RBAC before execution. Checking only the outer SQL string cannot restore the invariant. Add regression coverage for `query('SELECT * FROM read_parquet(...)')`, escaped-quote replacement scans, comments and whitespace around nested SQL, and a nested reference to a database unavailable to the token. The tests should assert rejection before the database sink, preserve the direct-reader and direct-RBAC controls, and verify that any intentionally supported safe `query()` form is authorized recursively on both `/api/v1/query` and `/api/v1/query/estimate`. ## Affected Package/Versions - Package: `github.com/basekick-labs/arc` (Go ecosystem). - Vulnerable tested revision: `9dda675b9032bf2331a07c1781ebf624f41c6cde`. - Current-head result: vulnerable at the same pinned revision. - Affected range: exact-tested-version only; no broader release or commit range is inferred. - Patched versions: none asserted because no fixed revision was tested. ## Advisory History The closest public Arc advisories address adjacent direct-syntax or endpoint surfaces, not this nested dynamic-SQL path: [GHSA-p2j4-c4g6-rpf5](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/security/advisories/GHSA-p2j4-c4g6-rpf5) covers direct DuckDB I/O functions; [GHSA-93cm-2v4m-c56c](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/security/advisories/GHSA-93cm-2v4m-c56c) covers the `parquet_scan` alias and other direct I/O functions; [GHSA-w8x2-cccw-25f7](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/security/advisories/GHSA-w8x2-cccw-25f7) covers bare-string replacement scans; and [GHSA-wmjj-g8xc-6hwr](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/security/advisories/GHSA-wmjj-g8xc-6hwr) covers a missing validator on the `GET /api/v1/query/:measurement` `where` parameter. The current public estimate-route authorization history includes [PR #487](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/pull/487), `fix(query): add RBAC permission checks to estimateQuery and listMeasurements`, and its related [estimateQuery RBAC fix commit](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/commit/a630ad88d59bd7f80e909b941c5dd4f018bbf7cc), which cover direct outer-query table-reference authorization. [PR #489](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/pull/489), `fix(api): add SHOW command RBAC-gating to estimateQuery endpoint`, its related [estimateQuery SHOW-gating fix commit](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/commit/4999df74027f264734413a0201ada08cf66af984), and [issue #488](https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc/issues/488), `estimateQuery does not RBAC-gate SHOW DATABASES/TABLES (count-only metadata leak)`, cover direct `SHOW` authorization and its tracked metadata leak. These records do not cover a SQL string parsed by DuckDB's `query()` after Arc's estimate-route validation and RBAC pass, so this nested `query()` inner-SQL path remains distinct and they do not close this fix surface. The bound report-history check found no prior submitted, ready-for-review, or completed-but-unsubmitted report for this exact nested `query()` estimate-route boundary. ## References - `internal/api/query.go:1409-1432` — route registration and read-auth/readiness gates. - `internal/api/query.go:1107-1315` — table-reference extraction and permission checking. - `internal/api/query.go:2164-2302` — SQL validation and direct filesystem/replacement-scan checks. - `internal/api/query.go:3944-4148` — estimate handler, outer transformation, count wrapper, and database sink. - `internal/api/retention.go:916-930` — direct Parquet read used by the nested-execution test. - `internal/api/query_rbac_test.go:375-409` — direct cross-database authorization control. - `internal/api/retention_test.go:217-260` — Parquet fixture and dry-run row/file assertions. - [DuckDB `query()` and `query_table()` table functions](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/guides/sql_features/query_and_query_table_functions). - [DuckDB utility functions](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/sql/functions/utility). ## Appendix A — Reproduction Helper Save this helper at `./patcher.go` in the repository/module root before running the attack command. GHSA-w8x2-cccw-25f7.title: DuckDB bare-string replacement scan bypasses the I/O function-name denylist and the RBAC table extractor
GHSA-w8x2-cccw-25f7.description: ## Summary This is an incomplete-fix residual of GHSA-93cm-2v4m-c56c (the query read-authorization anchor). Arc's DuckDB I/O denylist and its RBAC table extractor both key on DuckDB function names, but DuckDB resolves a bare single-quoted string in table position as a replacement scan with no function name. So an authenticated tenant reads any Parquet file inside the allow-listed storage root, including other tenants' databases, by writing `SELECT ... FROM '/path/to/another-db/*.parquet'`, bypassing the per-database RBAC the GHSA-93cm fix was meant to enforce. Executed with negative controls. It does not escape the DuckDB sandbox to arbitrary OS files; it is a within-allowlist cross-database read. ## The defect Confirmed at HEAD. The query-authorization pipeline defends against DuckDB reading arbitrary data by (a) a denylist of DuckDB I/O function names (read_parquet, read_csv, etc.) in ValidateSQLRequest (internal/api/query.go:2057, the function-name check at 2180), and (b) RBAC via extractTableReferences (query.go:1074), which parses out the referenced databases and measurements to check grants. Both key on function names. But DuckDB also resolves a bare single-quoted string in table position as a replacement scan with no function name: ```sql SELECT * FROM '/data/arc/db2/secrets/*.parquet' ``` This has no function name, so it passes the denylist, and extractTableReferences masks the quoted path to a bareword placeholder (`__STR_0__`) before matching, so RBAC never sees the foreign path. ## Attacker and reachability POST /api/v1/query with either form: - Comma/join form (needs only one legitimate grant): `{'sql':'SELECT b.s FROM cpu, '/data/arc/db2/secrets/*.parquet' b'}` - RBAC extracts only default.cpu (the caller has cpu:read), while the bare-string replacement scan reads db2's secrets. - Glob form (needs a database-wildcard grant): `{'sql':'SELECT * FROM '<storage-root>/*/**/*.parquet''}`. Attacker model: an authenticated tenant on an RBAC-enabled multi-tenant instance. Impact: read any Parquet within the allow-listed storage root, i.e. other tenants' data. It does not escape to arbitrary OS files; the DuckDB sandbox fix (internal/database/sandbox.go) holds. ## Verification Executed with negative controls. Two Go tests against the pinned DuckDB (duckdb-go/v2 v2.10501.0): DuckDB probes confirmed the bare-string replacement scan reads a foreign file inside the allow-list and is blocked outside it (so the sandbox fix stands); the Arc-layer test confirmed ValidateSQLRequest passes the bare-string forms while blocking the function forms, and that the comma-join extracts only default.cpu. Not verified: the full wired-HTTP integration with seeded RBAC (each of the three links is executed; only the glue is unproven). Notably, the maintainers' own otherwise-exhaustive denylist test matrix (query_test.go around 1030-1138) has no bare-string replacement-scan case; every existing I/O test uses a function name or COPY. ## Both anchor fixes are sound (this is a residual, not a regression) CVE-2026-48050 (the pprof/prefix auth bug) is closed in internal/auth/middleware.go:76-111. CVE-2026-47735 (arbitrary file read) is closed by the DuckDB sandbox plus the I/O function-name denylist. This finding is the replacement-scan path the function-name denylist does not cover. ## Suggested fix Do not rely on function names alone: extract and authorize every file path DuckDB will read, including bare single-quoted strings in table/FROM position (replacement scans), before executing. Concretely, make extractTableReferences resolve a quoted string in table position to a storage path and RBAC-check that path rather than masking it to a placeholder, and/or confine DuckDB's replacement-scan file access to the caller's authorized database directory only. Add the bare-string replacement-scan forms (comma and glob) to the denylist test matrix. ## Adjacent, not verified The compaction subprocess (internal/compaction/subprocess.go:101) runs an unsandboxed DuckDB, but on locally-downloaded temp copies with escapeSQLString on sort keys, so it looks closed; worth a dedicated ingest-side measurement-name pass. ## Tooling I used AI assistance while investigating. The bypass is executed-verified with two Go tests against the pinned DuckDB and negative controls (the bare-string scan reads a foreign in-allowlist file and is blocked outside it; ValidateSQLRequest passes the bare-string forms while blocking the function forms; the comma-join extracts only default.cpu), and I confirmed at HEAD that the denylist and extractTableReferences key on function names while a quoted path is masked to a placeholder.

GHSA-wmjj-g8xc-6hwr.title: Authenticated RBAC/tenant escape: query where-param bypasses DuckDB I/O-function denylist to read any database
GHSA-wmjj-g8xc-6hwr.description: ## Summary `GET /api/v1/query/:measurement` (`queryMeasurement`, `internal/api/query.go`) is the only user-SQL endpoint in Arc that never calls `ValidateSQLRequest`. Its sole guard on the user-controlled `where` query parameter is `validateWhereClauseQuery`, a keyword blocklist that does NOT block `SELECT` and does NOT block any DuckDB I/O table function (`read_parquet`, `parquet_scan`, `glob`, `read_csv`, `read_json`, `read_blob`, `parquet_metadata`). The `where` string is `fmt.Sprintf`-concatenated into `SELECT * FROM <db>.<meas> WHERE <where> ...` and executed on the shared DuckDB handle, whose sandbox allowlists the ENTIRE storage root. A token scoped to a single measurement's `read` permission can therefore read across the RBAC/tenant boundary via a scalar subquery that reads another tenant's Parquet files. This is the CVE-2026-55098 vulnerability class on a distinct, unpatched sibling endpoint. ## Root Cause The CVE-2026-55098 fix (commit `5dc8f53`) added the I/O-function denylist (`ioTableFunctionPattern`) inside `ValidateSQLRequest` only. `ValidateSQLRequest` guards the `POST /api/v1/query` (raw-SQL) path and the estimate path, but `queryMeasurement` never calls it. The `where` param instead flows only through `validateWhereClauseQuery` (`query.go:842`), which blocks `; -- /* */ DROP DELETE INSERT UPDATE TRUNCATE ALTER CREATE EXEC EXECUTE xp_ sp_ UNION` plus balanced-quote/paren checks — but neither `SELECT` nor any I/O table function. The RBAC check (`checkMeasurementPermission`) validates only the path-param `db.measurement`, never a foreign path inside the `where` subquery. The DuckDB sandbox (`sandbox.go buildAllowedDirectories`) still allowlists the whole `LocalStorageRoot` (not per-tenant) on HEAD, so every tenant's Parquet is reachable. ## Impact An authenticated token holding only a single measurement's `read` grant (in OSS auth-disabled deployments, an unauthenticated client) can read across the RBAC/tenant boundary: blind-boolean + error-based extraction (DuckDB errors returned verbatim at `query.go:4314`) plus `glob()`/`parquet_metadata()` schema and min/max enumeration of every database within the storage root. RBAC-scope escape / cross-tenant confidentiality breach. ## Proof of Concept `GET /api/v1/query/cpu?database=default&where=<payload>` with a token holding only `default.cpu:read`. PoC-correction note (verified): the naive `**/*.parquet` glob payload contains the substring `/*` which IS on the blocklist and is REJECTED. Use `parquet_scan(`/`glob(` (NOT `read_parquet(`, which triggers a `getTransformedSQL` fast-path at `query.go:2513` that skips transformation) with a path that never places `/` immediately before `*`. Verified-passing payloads: - `time > (SELECT max(value) FROM parquet_scan('/data/arc/secretdb/cpu/data_0001.parquet'))` - `time > (SELECT count(*) FROM glob('/data/arc/secretdb/cpu/d.parquet'))` ## Attack Chain 1. Entry: `GET /api/v1/query/cpu?database=default&where=<payload>` — Action: attacker with only `default.cpu:read` sends the request. Guard: `readAuth` → `RequireRead` + `checkMeasurementPermission(default,cpu,read)` (`query.go:1418`,`4267`). Bypass proof: legitimately satisfied — this is the attacker's own grant; RBAC only inspects `default.cpu`, never the foreign path inside `where`. 2. Guard: `validateWhereClauseQuery(where)` (`query.go:4256`→`842`) — Bypass proof: executing the blocklist in Go against `time > (SELECT max(value) FROM parquet_scan('/data/arc/secretdb/cpu/data_0001.parquet'))` returns nil (passes): `SELECT` not in `dangerousQueryPatterns`, `parquet_scan` not listed, quotes balanced (2), parens balanced (2), no `;`/`--`/`/*`/`UNION`. 3. Guard MISSING: `ValidateSQLRequest` / `ioTableFunctionPattern` — Bypass proof: grep confirms `ioTableFunctionPattern` is referenced only inside `ValidateSQLRequest` (`query.go:2200`); `queryMeasurement` contains no `ValidateSQLRequest` call (verified on HEAD and on `git show v26.06.3:internal/api/query.go`). 4. Sink: `sql = 'SELECT * FROM default.cpu WHERE ' + where + ' ORDER BY ...'` (`query.go:4277-4283`) → `getTransformedSQL` → `h.db.Query(...)` (`query.go:4308`). Bypass proof: `MaskStringLiterals` protects the inner `'/path'`; outer `default.cpu` rewrites while `parquet_scan(...)` subquery survives executable; sandbox allowlists whole storage root (`sandbox.go`). 5. Impact: blind-boolean + error-based oracle + `glob()`/`parquet_metadata()` enumeration across every tenant within the storage root. ## Bypass Evidence - `validateWhereClauseQuery` executed in Go against the corrected payload → passes (SELECT and parquet_scan not blocked). - `git show 5dc8f53 -- internal/api/query.go` = single hunk inside `func ValidateSQLRequest`; diff mentions `queryMeasurement` 0 times, `validateWhereClauseQuery` 0 times. - The sink is proven by CVE-2026-55098's own PoC (`poc_sandbox_alias_bypass.py`) which demonstrates `parquet_scan()` reading cross-tenant within the same whole-root sandbox on the DuckDB version Arc pins. ## Affected Versions `<= 26.06.3` — present on the latest release tag `v26.06.3` (verified `git show v26.06.3:internal/api/query.go`); no fix in `v26.06.3..HEAD` touching `queryMeasurement`/`validateWhereClauseQuery`. ## Suggested Fix Route the `where`-clause path through `ValidateSQLRequest` (or at minimum apply `ioTableFunctionPattern` to the `where` fragment), and/or scope the DuckDB sandbox `allowed_directories` per-tenant so a subquery cannot read outside the caller's authorized measurement path. --- Reported by **zx (Jace)** — GitHub: @manus-use

GHSA-wwfh-qrfq-6f8g.title: Arc Enterprise Raft consensus transport lacks app-layer auth, enabling admin-token forgery and cluster compromise
GHSA-wwfh-qrfq-6f8g.description: ## Summary Arc's Raft consensus transport has no application-layer authentication. When `cluster.tls_enabled` is false (the default) the transport is plaintext `raft.NewTCPTransport`; even with TLS enabled, the custom StreamLayer (`raft_stream.go`) is a pure TLS wrapper that adds NO HMAC/shared-secret check, and client-certificate verification is only required when `tls_ca_file` is set (default empty). The cluster's mandated `shared_secret` — enforced on the replication, join, heartbeat and leave channels — is NEVER consulted on the Raft path. Any peer that can reach the Raft bind port (`:9200` default) can speak the consensus protocol and drive `ClusterFSM.Apply`, including `CommandCreateToken` to mint an admin token and achieve full cluster compromise. ## Root Cause `raft/node.go:171-184` selects `NewTCPTransport` (plaintext) when `TLSConfig == nil`, else `NewTLSStreamLayer` (TLS-only, no HMAC). `cluster.tls_enabled` defaults false (`config.go:1719`); `RequireAndVerifyClientCert` is set only when `tls_ca_file != ''` (`tls.go:63`), default empty (`config.go:1722`). `grep -riE 'SharedSecret|HMAC'` across `internal/cluster/raft/` and `raft_stream.go` finds only one unrelated comment — the `shared_secret` that authenticates every other cluster channel (`coordinator.go:540/784/911/1089/1250/1280/1335/1466`) is absent on the Raft path. Post-CVE-2026-55678, clustering refuses to start without `shared_secret` (`main.go:1431` `os.Exit(1)`), so the operative fully-compliant deployment is secret-set + TLS-off (default) — every channel authenticated EXCEPT Raft. `ClusterFSM.Apply` (`fsm.go:765`) dispatches `applyCreateToken` (`fsm.go:795`); `validateTokenEntry` is shape-only and `validatePermissionString` explicitly allows `'admin'`. ## Impact A network peer with a position on the cluster interconnect (compromised sibling pod/container, mis-scoped security group, or a MitM position when TLS is on but `tls_ca_file` is empty) can inject a forged higher-term `AppendEntries` carrying `Command{Type: CommandCreateToken, permissions:['admin']}`. The follower adopts the higher term, appends, and applies the entry; the token materializes into local SQLite (`main.go:1512`) and is usable as an admin credential on that node's public API. Full cluster compromise (also `applyPromoteWriter`, `applyRegisterFile`, `applyDeleteFile`). Confidentiality + integrity + availability. ## Proof of Concept Against a clustered Arc node (default `cluster.tls_enabled=false`), connect to the Raft port (`:9200`) and drive the hashicorp/raft NetworkTransport wire protocol: send an `AppendEntries` RPC with `Term` greater than the current term and log entries encoding `Command{Type: CommandCreateToken}` with an admin `CreateTokenPayload` (PBKDF2 hash + prefix + `permissions:['admin']`). On `LeaderCommit` advance the follower applies it via `ClusterFSM.Apply → applyCreateToken`. Authenticate to the public API with the minted token. ## Attack Chain 1. Entry: attacker reaches the Raft interconnect port `:9200` (sibling container, mis-scoped SG) or holds a MitM position when `tls_enabled=true` + `tls_ca_file=''`. Guard: network segmentation / TLS. Bypass proof: plaintext default has none (`config.go:1719`); TLS-without-CA requires no client cert (`tls.go:63`). 2. Speak the Raft protocol to a follower. Guard: (should be) shared-secret HMAC as on every other channel. Bypass proof: `TLSStreamLayer`/`NewTCPTransport` hand the raw conn to hashicorp/raft; no `SharedSecret`/HMAC on the Raft path (grep-confirmed); NetworkTransport delegates all peer auth to the StreamLayer. 3. Inject `AppendEntries` (term > current) carrying `Command{Type: CommandCreateToken, permissions:['admin']}`. Guard: FSM-side `validateTokenEntry` (`fsm.go`). Bypass proof: validates entry SHAPE, not ORIGIN; `validatePermissionString` explicitly allows `'admin'`; origin auth was supposed to live at the (unauthenticated) transport. 4. Impact: token replicated as a real cluster token → authenticate to the public API as admin → full cluster compromise. ## Bypass Evidence - `git show 2e7902f --stat` (CVE-2026-48106 replication HMAC) and `git show 38402ad --stat` (CVE-2026-55678 coordinator HMAC + fail-closed secret): neither touches `internal/cluster/raft/node.go` nor `internal/cluster/security/raft_stream.go`. - `grep -riE 'SharedSecret|HMAC' internal/cluster/raft/ raft_stream.go` → only one unrelated comment; `shared_secret` never consulted on the Raft path. - `validateTokenEntry` / `validatePermissionString` confirmed shape-only and `'admin'`-permitting. Note: hashicorp/raft v1.6.0 was not in the local module cache, so the 'follower applies a forged higher-term entry' step rests on documented NetworkTransport behavior (mTLS is its only peer-auth mechanism) plus Arc's own deliberate HMAC-hardening of every other channel — strong support, verified by inference rather than a line-level library trace. ## Affected Versions `<= 26.06.3` (Arc Enterprise clustering feature) — present on the latest release tag; no fix in `v26.06.3..HEAD` touching the Raft transport. ## Suggested Fix Apply the mandated `shared_secret` HMAC to the Raft StreamLayer (as done for the replication/coordinator channels, working 'even without TLS'), or mandate mTLS (`RequireAndVerifyClientCert` + configured CA) whenever clustering is enabled — fail closed if neither is configured. --- Reported by **zx (Jace)** — GitHub: @manus-use

Prior to version 26.06.1, Arc's user-SQL validator (`internal/api/query.go:ValidateSQLRequest`) blocked only `read_parquet(` and `arc_partition_agg(` via regex denylist. Prior to the repository-verified 26.06.2 repair, the remediation of `CVE-2026-47735` leaves a cross-database authorization bypass through DuckDB table-valued I/O functions. In `internal/database/sandbox.go`, `allowed_directories` uses `cfg.LocalStorageRoot`, configured by `storage.local_path`, while `enable_external_access=false` blocks access outside that entire multi-tenant root. `GetStoragePath` in `internal/storage/util.go` stores all databases beneath it. In `internal/api/query.go`, `extractTableReferences` skips names followed by an opening parenthesis and `checkQueryPermissions` allows queries with no extracted table references, including tokens with `permissions: []`. The `userSQLReadParquetPattern` denylist catches literal `read_parquet(` and the earlier protection also blocks `arc_partition_agg(`, but misses the `parquet_scan` alias and `glob`, `parquet_metadata`, `parquet_schema`, `read_blob`, `read_csv_auto`, `read_json` and `read_text`.
